question: What defines the medicalisation of female genital mutilation?

options.A: Performing the procedure using sterile instruments in a hospital
options.B: Administering general anesthesia during traditional ceremonies
options.C: Treating the physical complications resulting from the procedure
options.D: Surgical reconstruction of the genital organs after trauma

explanation: Medicalisation refers specifically to healthcare providers performing FGM procedures, regardless of whether it is done in a clinic or using sterile tools. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h1)

question: Why do international health organisations strongly oppose the medicalisation of FGM?

options.A: It increases the risk of surgical site infections due to hospital-acquired pathogens
options.B: It legitimises a human rights violation and fails to eliminate physical and psychological harm
options.C: It places an unnecessary financial burden on public healthcare infrastructure
options.D: It violates international trade agreements regarding pharmaceutical distribution

explanation: Involving health professionals normalises the practice and falsely implies that it is medically safe, while ignoring the ongoing trauma and complications. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h1)

question: What is a primary financial motivation for some healthcare workers to perform medicalised FGM?

options.A: Funding community health outreach programs independently
options.B: Purchasing advanced medical equipment for their clinics
options.C: Receiving government bonuses for meeting surgical quotas
options.D: Supplementing low income in resource-constrained environments

explanation: Economic pressures and poor remuneration in certain healthcare sectors drive some professionals to perform the procedure for quick cash payments. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h2)

question: A nurse agrees to perform a ritual nick on a newborn to prevent the family from seeking a traditional circumciser. What underlying rationale influences this decision?

options.A: Desire to document epidemiological data on cultural practices
options.B: Harm reduction based on the belief that clinical settings are safer
options.C: Adherence to evidence-based obstetric clinical practice guidelines
options.D: Compliance with mandatory national public health immunization laws

explanation: Practitioners often rationalise their involvement through a flawed harm-reduction mindset, assuming clinical conditions prevent severe complications. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h2)

question: Which classification of FGM involves the narrowing of the vaginal orifice through the creation of a covering seal?
explanation: Type III, also known as infibulation, involves cutting and repositioning the labia to create a restrictive seal over the vagina. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h3)

question: What is a common misconception held by clinicians who perform symbolic or minimal cuts during FGM?

options.A: Symbolic cuts stimulate hormonal balance and improve reproductive fertility
options.B: Removing less tissue completely eliminates all psychological and physical risks
options.C: Minor incisions heal faster without requiring any antiseptic intervention
options.D: Patients will forget the procedure due to developing childhood amnesia

explanation: Any intentional alteration of healthy genital tissue carries risks of chronic pain, infection, and psychological distress, regardless of the volume of tissue removed. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h3)

question: Which complication is most frequently encountered during childbirth by women who have undergone FGM?

options.A: Obstructed labor and severe perineal trauma
options.B: Spontaneous rupture of the uterine corpus
options.C: Complete cessation of placental hormone production
options.D: Premature closure of the fetal neural tube

explanation: Scar tissue and narrowing from genital mutilation frequently obstruct the birth canal, leading to prolonged labor and severe tearing. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h4)

question: A patient presents with chronic pelvic pain and painful dysmenorrhea years after undergoing childhood FGM. What pathophysiological factor is the most likely contributor?

options.A: Neuroma formation and dense scar tissue entrapment of nerve endings
options.B: Persistent low-grade systemic autoimmune inflammatory response
options.C: Hormonal imbalances caused by premature ovarian failure
options.D: Chronic ascending fungal infections of the fallopian tubes

explanation: The healing of severed nerve endings often results in painful neuromas and extensive scarring that generate chronic pelvic discomfort. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h4)

question: Which bioethical principle is directly violated when a healthcare professional performs medicalised FGM?
explanation: Non-maleficence requires healthcare providers to avoid causing physical or psychological harm to patients, which FGM directly violates. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h5)

question: What legal consequence typically awaits a registered nurse found guilty of performing FGM in countries with active anti-FGM laws?

options.A: Criminal prosecution, imprisonment, and permanent revocation of the nursing license
options.B: Temporary reassignment to non-clinical administrative duties for six months
options.C: A minor administrative warning letter placed in the professional employment file
options.D: Mandatory enrollment in an ethics refresher course without license suspension

explanation: Medicalised FGM is treated as a serious criminal offense, carrying severe legal penalties and professional disbarment for licensed practitioners. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h5)

question: What is an effective community health nursing strategy to combat FGM without driving the practice underground?

options.A: Engaging local leaders and promoting non-harmful alternative rites of passage
options.B: Imposing immediate mandatory police raids on all traditional village ceremonies
options.C: Withholding routine maternal healthcare from uncooperative communities
options.D: Publicly shaming families who express intent to perform the procedure

explanation: Collaborative community engagement and alternative ceremonies respect cultural transition needs while eliminating physical harm. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h6)

question: Why is a trauma-informed approach essential when providing care for survivors of FGM in a clinical setting?

options.A: It replaces the need for surgical intervention in cases of severe infibulation
options.B: It ensures the patient can immediately undergo corrective reconstructive surgery
options.C: It minimizes retraumatisation during physical examinations and builds therapeutic trust
options.D: It completely reverses the anatomical alterations caused by the initial procedure

explanation: Survivors often experience anxiety and fear during pelvic exams; trauma-informed care prioritizes safety, consent, and emotional reassurance. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h6)
